title: Suresh Garments v. Fashion House
text: The plaintiff, Suresh Garments, claims specific performance and damages for breach of contract against the defendant, Fashion House. The parties executed a franchise agreement for a consideration of Rs 50,00,000. After the plaintiff paid the full consideration and invested in the franchise setup, the defendant unilaterally terminated the agreement without cause. The plaintiff sought specific performance or in the alternative damages. The court holds that specific performance of a franchise agreement is not feasible as it requires co-operation and trust between the parties, which is absent after acrimonious termination. However, the breach of contract entitles the plaintiff to substantial damages. The damages include the consideration paid, infrastructure investment made in reliance on the contract, and loss of anticipated profits for the agreed term. Total damages of Rs 2,20,00,000 are awarded for breach of contract. Interest at 10% per annum is added.
